summary: Overall, your report is competent but flawed: it covers all major mission elements with STK evidence and a coherent design, but technical gaps (launch dogleg, unflown vehicle, table errors, no link budget) and weak referencing/presentation reduce the mark. Focus next on resolving launch/orbit consistency, adding link-budget/table accuracy and software files, and fixing presentation/referencing.
next_steps: Resolve launch/orbit consistency: justify Vega E availability or choose an operational vehicle; discuss the Kourou-to-SSO dogleg/plane change and correct the 'two launch windows per day' claim.
Add a link budget/data-rate analysis and clean the STK access table (remove duplicate row 15, fix row 6 inconsistency); include software files and size the drag sail with 25-year deorbit compliance.
Fix presentation and referencing: number figures and label tables, replace bare URLs with full citations, remove Wikipedia [6], and proofread grammar (e.g. 'a Earth', 'complied', 'purposed').

criteria.C1: Your Introduction clearly states the coral-reef/ocean monitoring mission, rationale (bleaching/GBR), single-spacecraft justification, and users (CSIRO/BOM, government/university), supported by [1]–[4]. To strengthen toward the top of Accomplished, tighten weak referencing and ensure every claim has a specific source.
criteria.C2: Your Mission Design addresses launch, orbit, ground control, duration and EOL with STK screenshots and an inclination plot. Gaps noted: Vega E is unflown; Kourou-to-SSO dogleg/plane change is not discussed; STK access table has duplicate row 15 and inconsistent row 6; no link budget/data-rate analysis; software files missing; Wikipedia used for launch data. For Accomplished, resolve these and support all major requirements with quality evidence (software files, hand calculations, literature).
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion reaches specific points on launch, orbit and ground station, e.g. the polar SSO rationale. However, it omits mission duration and EOL outcomes and is somewhat generic. To reach Accomplished, draw detailed and appropriate conclusions from all evidence in the report, including duration, EOL/deorbit compliance, and communications performance.
criteria.C4: Your report has clear headings and readable prose, but grammar errors ('a Earth', 'complied', 'purposed'), figures lack numbers, tables are unlabelled, bibliography is bare URLs, and Wikipedia is cited [6]. To reach Accomplished, provide a professional engineering report structure: consistent formatting, numbered/labelled figures and tables, proofread language, and full citations matching the reference list with no Wikipedia.
